**ADICIONAR SEÇÃO DE MATERIAL**

**Ultimate durability meets modern aesthetics**

Quartz countertops combine approximately 90% ground natural quartz crystals with 10% polymer resins and pigments. The result is an ultra-durable, non-porous surface that rivals natural stone in strength while offering complete stain and scratch resistance without annual sealing.

* **Zero sealing required:** Unlike granite or marble, quartz is non-porous. Bacteria, liquid spills, oils, and food acids cannot penetrate the surface, making it extremely hygienic and easy to sanitize.  
* **Vast style & color selection:** From realistic marble veining (Calacatta and Carrara styles) to sleek industrial concrete looks and solid modern tones, quartz offers consistent color control across entire slab runs.  
* **World-class slab brands:** We source directly from leading engineered stone manufacturers, including Cambria, Caesarstone, Silestone, MSI Surfaces, and Cosentino, giving you access to top-tier factory warranties and direct pricing.  
* **Ideal applications:** Perfect for busy family kitchen islands, high-traffic commercial bar tops, bathroom vanities, and rental unit renovations where low maintenance is mandatory.

**ADICIONAR SEÇÃO DE FAQ**

**Frequently asked questions**

**Do quartz countertops require routine sealing?**  
No. Quartz is entirely non-porous due to its resin-bound composition. It never requires sealing, polishing powders, or special oil treatments throughout its lifespan.

**Can you place hot pans directly on quartz counters?**  
While quartz is heat-resistant, rapid extreme temperature changes can damage the resin binders (thermal shock). We always recommend using trivets or hot pads under high-heat cookware.

**How does quartz pricing compare to granite?**   
Entry-level quartz and mid-tier granite fall into similar price brackets per square foot. Premium veined quartz (such as dramatic Calacatta patterns) sits at a similar investment level to high-end exotic natural stone, but offers significantly lower long-term maintenance costs.

**How do you conceal seams in large quartz kitchen islands?**   
We use digital laser templating to plan cut layouts around your cabinet layout. Our fabricators use color-matched epoxy resins to join slabs, resulting in tight, barely visible seams.

**ADICIONAR SEÇÃO DE MATERIAL**

**The intersection of luxury and strength**

Quartzite is a 100% natural metamorphic rock formed deep within the earth when sandstone is subjected to extreme heat and pressure. This natural process fuses the quartz grains together, creating an incredibly dense, hard stone that frequently features the sweeping, elegant veining traditionally associated with marble.

**Unmatched natural hardness:** Quartzite actually ranks higher on the Mohs scale of hardness than granite. It is highly resistant to scratching, chipping, and daily wear-and-tear, making it ideal for active culinary spaces.

**The marble aesthetic without the compromise:** Many homeowners desire the soft white and grey veining of Carrara or Calacatta marble but want to avoid its fragility. Quartzite provides this exact aesthetic profile but with structural integrity meant for heavy use.

**Heat & UV resistance:** Because it is formed by extreme geological heat, natural quartzite handles hot pots and pans exceptionally well. It is also UV resistant, meaning it will not fade in sun-drenched kitchens or outdoor patio applications.

**Slab authenticity:** Because quartzite is a natural stone, no two slabs are exactly alike. Your kitchen island or bathroom vanity will feature a completely unique, organic geological pattern that cannot be replicated in a factory.

**ADICIONAR SEÇÃO DE FAQ**

**Frequently asked questions**

**What is the difference between Quartzite and Quartz?**

This is the most common point of confusion. Quartzite is a 100% natural rock mined from the earth in blocks and cut into slabs. Quartz (engineered quartz) is a man-made product created in a factory by mixing crushed stone with resin and pigments. Quartzite is highly heat-resistant but requires sealing; engineered quartz is non-porous (no sealing) but is sensitive to high heat.

**Does quartzite require sealing?**

Yes. Like granite and all natural stones, quartzite is porous. We apply a professional-grade sealer upon installation to protect against liquid absorption and staining. You should reseal your quartzite countertops approximately once a year to maintain optimal stain resistance.

**Will quartzite etch like marble?**

True quartzite will not etch from everyday kitchen acids (like lemon juice or vinegar) the way marble does. However, because stones are labeled somewhat loosely in the global supply chain, some "soft quartzites" share properties with marble. We source directly from trusted suppliers and verify the density of our slabs to ensure you get true quartzite durability.

**How long does fabrication take after templating?**

Once you have selected your specific slab and our team has completed the digital laser templating of your cabinets, fabrication generally takes 5 to 7 business days. The actual on-site installation is completed in a single day.

**ADICIONAR SEÇÃO DE MATERIAL**

**Unmatched timeless elegance**

Marble has been the standard for luxury architecture and interior design for centuries. Formed from limestone subjected to extreme heat and pressure, this natural stone is renowned for its luminous surface and distinct, flowing veining patterns.

**Classic aesthetic:** No engineered stone can perfectly replicate the genuine depth and organic veining of natural marble varieties like Calacatta, Carrara, and Statuario. Each slab is a unique piece of geological art.

**Naturally cool surface:** Because marble remains naturally cool to the touch, it is the premier surface choice for serious bakers and pastry chefs working with dough.

**Ideal applications:** Due to its softer composition, marble is highly sought after for master bathroom vanities, fireplace surrounds, shower walls, and low-traffic baking stations where its aesthetic can be showcased.

**Care and aging:** Marble is a porous natural stone that will patinate over time. It requires regular sealing and immediate attention to spills (especially acids like lemon or wine) to prevent etching and staining. For many homeowners, this natural "living finish" is part of the stone's authentic charm.

**ADICIONAR SEÇÃO DE FAQ**

**Frequently asked questions**

**Is marble a good choice for a busy family kitchen?**

While beautiful, marble is softer and more porous than granite or quartz. It is susceptible to etching from acidic foods (like citrus, vinegar, and tomato sauce) and can stain if spills are not wiped up quickly. If you have a highly active kitchen and want low maintenance, we generally recommend Quartzite or engineered Quartz. If you embrace the natural patina and aging of stone, marble is a stunning choice.

**How often do I need to seal my marble countertops?**

To maintain maximum stain resistance, natural marble countertops should be professionally sealed upon installation, and resealed by the homeowner every 6 to 12 months, depending on the volume of daily use.

**What is the difference between Carrara and Calacatta marble?**

Both are premium Italian marbles, but they have distinct looks. Carrara typically features a softer, greyer background with fine, feathery veining. Calacatta is generally rarer, featuring a brighter white background with bold, dramatic, and thicker veining.

**How long does the process take?**

After you select your marble slab and we complete the digital templating of your space, fabrication takes about 5 to 7 business days. Our crews will then complete the on-site installation in a single day.

**ADICIONAR SEÇÃO DE MATERIAL**

**Maximum strength and timeless geological character**

Granite is a 100% natural igneous rock formed deep within the earth under intense heat and pressure over millions of years. Composed of quartz, feldspar, and mica, granite is one of the hardest natural materials on earth, offering an ideal balance of structural toughness, heat resistance, and unique organic beauty.

**Exceptional heat resistance:** Unlike engineered materials with resin binders, natural granite can easily withstand hot pots, pans, and baking dishes placed directly on its surface without scorching or discoloring.

**Scratch & wear resistance:** Highly resistant to everyday kitchen knives, heavy utensils, and high-volume daily use. It is the premier natural stone for busy family kitchens, commercial bars, and outdoor grilling stations.

**100% unique geological patterns:** Every granite slab features distinct mineral specks, deep crystalline structures, and natural veining. No two installations will ever look identical.

**Low maintenance protection:** When properly treated with a penetrating stone sealer, granite resists water penetration, oil absorption, and common kitchen stains while remaining simple to clean with basic warm water and soap.

**ADICIONAR SEÇÃO DE FAQ**

**Frequently asked questions**

**Is granite completely heat resistant?**  
Yes. Granite naturally forms under extreme geothermal temperatures, making it inherently heat-proof. You can place hot pots, pans, and baking sheets directly onto granite surfaces without causing scorching or thermal shock damage.

**How often do granite countertops need to be sealed?**  
Granite is a porous natural stone, but applying a professional penetrating sealer prevents liquid absorption. We seal every granite surface during installation. For ongoing protection, homeowners should reapply a simple spray-on sealer once every 12 to 18 months.

**Can granite be installed outdoors?**  
Yes. Unlike quartz (which can fade or yellow under direct UV sunlight due to resin binders), natural granite is 100% UV-resistant and weatherproof. It is the leading natural stone choice for outdoor kitchens, patio bar tops, and BBQ surrounds.

**How long does fabrication and installation take?**   
After slab selection and digital laser templating are completed, custom fabrication takes approximately 5 to 7 business days. On-site installation is completed in a single day by our insured installation crew.
